C: › a wooden bar that is fastened over the necks of two animals, especially cattle, and connected to the vehicle or load that they are pulling
› a fitted part of a piece of clothing, especially a strip that goes around the shoulders or waist, to which is sewn a looser piece of material
› formal something that connects two things or people, usually in a way that unfairly limits freedom
紐帶，聯結；（通常指）束縛，枷鎖

T: › [ T ] to put a yoke on animals, especially cattle, so that they are fastened together and to a connected vehicle or load

T often passive: › [ T often passive ] formal to combine or connect two things

example: Both countries had thrown off the communist yoke.
兩國都已經擺脫了共產主義的枷鎖。
Two oxen yoked to a plough walked wearily up and down the field.
兩頭用軛套在犁上的公牛在吃力地來回耕地。
All these different political elements have somehow been yoked together to form a new alliance.
所有這些不同的政治力量不知怎地結成了一個新的聯盟。

NONE: › a stupid or awkward person who lives in the countryside rather than a town, especially one whose appearance is in some way strange or humorous
（尤指外表可笑的）土包子，鄉巴佬

example: He plays the country yokel in the butter ad.
他在奶油廣告中扮演鄉巴佬。
